messages:
maya: Heads-up — seeing a bunch of missing child spans for /v1/generate in prod since ~02:10 UTC. Parent spans exist but children often empty. Anyone else
aj: yep, noticed a latency spike and this in ingest-service logs: `DroppedSpans=47 backpressure=true exporter_buffer_full=true`
ingest-bot: alert: trace_exporter_queue_utilization=94% cluster=prod-eu
leo: pulled otel-collector logs from the canary: 
```
2026-03-18T02:11:02Z error exporter/otlpexporter failed to push: rpc error: code=ResourceExhausted desc="queue full"
2026-03-18T02:11:03Z warn exporter/otlpexporter drop_spans=23 reason=queue_full
```
sam: did we change any blob-shipper or kafka producer config in last deploy? I remember a PR about batching
aj: we bumped producer batch_size last night (https://git/repo/commit/ab12...) — 100 -> 1000 to optimize throughput for embeddings
maya: hmm that would increase memory queued in collector if downstream can't keep up
leo: also seeing `kafka_producer.queue.size` spike to capacity in metrics (~100k messages queued)
aj: reproducer from staging: when exporter backpressures, the collector currently drops spans once internal queue > threshold. Not ideal.
sam: we should avoid silent drops. Quick mitigations: reduce batch_size, enable retries/backoff on otel exporter, and throttle request routing to ingest pool
aj: rolling a canary patch to configmap now: reduce batch_size to 200 and enable `retry_on_failure` + small backoff
```
# otel_collector.yaml snippet
exporters:
  otlp:
    retry_on_failure:
      enabled: true
      initial_interval: 200ms
      max_interval: 5s
      max_elapsed_time: 30s
service:
  pipelines:
    traces:
      receivers: [otlp]
      exporters: [otlp]
```
aj: applied to prod-eu subset (canary) at 02:22 UTC
sre-bot: incident created: INC-2026-0298 "trace exporter queue saturation" — severity=P2 assigned=ingest-team
leo: metrics after canary: trace_exporter_queue_utilization dropped -> 28% in the canary nodes
aj: logs show `drop_spans` count decreased to 0 in canary, and parent->child relationships restored in sampled traces :tada:
maya: verifying in console — child spans showing up again for previously affected traces. Good catch.
sam: next steps: follow-up fix — implement a bounded buffer with backpressure propagation to ingress (so we return 503 instead of dropping), and add SLO for dropped spans + alerting rule for ResourceExhausted errors
leo: i'll open a ticket for the long-term fix and coordinate with infra for collector memory bump and producer tuning
aj: also propose adding a telemetry sanity check in the deploy pipeline that looks for `drop_spans` logs in the first 10m after rollout
maya: please add postmortem once stable. For now keep the canary config for 1h then sweep if steady
sam: noted, assigning postmortem to @leo and @aj.
ingest-bot: note: temporary canary rollback plan in place if queue_utilization > 80% for 5m
aj: monitoring — so far 25m stable in canary, will continue to watch. Thanks all.
